title: Attack and defend: cross-site scripting
blurb: Understand reflected and stored XSS, find it in logs, and stop it with output encoding and a content security policy.
scenario: Users of the company's support portal report pop-ups and being logged out unexpectedly. A comment on a support ticket seems to be involved. Investigate cross-site scripting (XSS) and harden the portal.
objectives: Tell reflected, stored and DOM-based XSS apart
Apply the fixes in the right places

steps.title: Types of XSS
steps.learn: In **XSS**, attacker-supplied script runs in **another user's browser**, in the context of the trusted site. From there it can steal session cookies or act as the user.
steps.task: Match each case to its XSS type.

fields.label: Script saved in a ticket comment runs for everyone who opens the ticket
Script in a link's search parameter is echoed back in the results page
The page's own JavaScript writes the URL fragment into the page

steps.title: Spot it
steps.question: Which saved ticket comment shows an XSS attempt?

options.text: The printer on floor 3 shows error 0x8007.

steps.title: Fix it
steps.learn: The main fix is **context-aware output encoding**: when the page shows user text, `<` becomes `<` and so on, so the browser shows it as text instead of running it. A **Content-Security-Policy** header limits where scripts can come from, and **HttpOnly** cookies can't be read by script at all.
steps.task: Pick the setting for each protection.

fields.label: Ticket comments are shown with
options: A blocklist of the word script

steps.title: Why not a blocklist?
steps.question: Why isn't removing the word "script" from comments enough?

options.text: Script can run without a script tag, for example through event attributes such as onerror, and filters are easy to dodge with different case or encodings. Encoding the output handles every case.
It is enough, because XSS always needs a script tag.
options.why: Event handlers, javascript: URLs and other contexts can all run code.

summary: Stored, reflected and DOM-based XSS, a stored payload in a ticket comment, output encoding as the main fix, plus a CSP header and HttpOnly cookies, and why blocklists fail.
